items.title: Ambient locally finite mod-two relative chains for candidate regions
items.design_state: Step 2 owner-authorized same-pair local proof; source release recorded, ordinary native gates pending.
items.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and $B\subseteq\Sigma$ closed. Use $\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo two. A chain in $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)$ is a formal sum of continuous singular $k$-simplex maps with mod-two coefficients such that every point of $\Sigma$ has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many nonzero simplex images. Put $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)=0$ for $k<0$. Let $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma;B)$ be the subgroup of these **ambient** chains whose simplex images are contained in $B$, and set
$$C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma,B):=C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)/C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma;B).$$
The face boundary, with all signs equal to plus in $\mathbb Z_2$, is well-defined and locally finite, preserves the $B$-supported subgroup, and induces $\bar\partial^2=0$ on this quotient. Define
$$H_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma,B):=\ker\bar\partial_k/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_{k+1}.$$
For ambient locally finite chains $a,x$ with boundaries supported in $B$, the equality $[a]=[x]$ holds exactly when there is $r\in C_{k+1}^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)$ with $\partial r+a+x\in C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma;B)$. Changing representatives by quotient boundaries or $B$-supported chains preserves this criterion. Finite ordinary chains are allowed; on compact $\Sigma$ this is precisely the ordinary relative singular chain model.

Here is an explicit meaning of supplied fundamental-chain data. Let $Y\subseteq\Sigma$ be an embedded $n$-manifold with boundary, $n\ge1$. An **ambient locally finite mod-two fundamental chain for $Y$** is a chain $c\in C_n^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)$ whose simplex maps land in $Y$, whose boundary maps land in $\partial Y$, and which satisfies the following local condition. For each $p\in Y\setminus\partial Y$, retain the finitely many simplices of $c$ whose images contain $p$, obtaining an ordinary finite chain $c_p$ in $Y$. Its class in $H_n(Y,Y\setminus\{p\};\mathbb Z_2)$ is the unique nonzero element. The boundary of $c_p$ avoids $p$, so this class is defined. The local group is $\mathbb Z_2$, without an orientation choice. These are explicit conditions on supplied chains, not an assertion that arbitrary nonproper embeddings push intrinsic locally finite chains into $\Sigma$.

A sufficient construction is as follows. Supply a pure $n$-dimensional ordered-vertex locally finite triangulation of $Y$, with boundary a subcomplex, whose realized simplex maps into $\Sigma$ form a locally finite family. Proper inclusion of a locally finite triangulated $Y$ into $\Sigma$ is sufficient for this ambient condition. Require that each interior codimension-one face has two incident top simplices and each boundary face has one. For every interior point $p$, supply a finite subcomplex neighborhood $N_p$ which is a compact $n$-manifold with boundary, with $p$ in its interior, such that the sum of its parametrized top simplices represents its compact mod-two relative fundamental class. A compact manifold ball or star with its verified relative fundamental chain supplies such a local certificate; no claim about an arbitrary triangulation's local stars is made. Then the sum of **all** top simplices, parametrized in the supplied vertex order, is an ambient locally finite fundamental chain for $Y$. For a supplied triangulated region whose boundary faces are divided into the $a$-faces, the $x$-faces and faces supported in $B$, this construction gives the displayed relative-chain criterion directly. No existence of a triangulation, a region, a chain certificate or an admissible candidate is asserted.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, relative chains and manifold local homology
references.locator: The existing pinned relative-chain and local-homology suppliers are used below. The ambient locally finite quotient and the sufficient construction with supplied local certificates are proved locally; no new external full-text reading is claimed.

items.title: Regulated generalized entropy for AdS candidate surfaces
items.physical_scope: A model definition for finite-regulator generalized entropy on a supplied class of spacelike codimension-two bulk surfaces with fixed boundary anchor and homology class. It assigns a renormalized value only when the named combined sequence converges finitely in its fixed scheme. It asserts no candidate existence, convergence, scheme independence, gravitational field equation, entropy dictionary, or monotonicity law.

references.title: Ahmed Almheiri, Thomas Hartman, Juan Maldacena, Edgar Shaghoulian, and Amirhossein Tajdini, The entropy of Hawking radiation, §§6 and 8
references.locator: Full-text review; §§6 and 8, equations (6.2) and (8.2), for area plus regulated semiclassical bulk entropy on a surface and its associated region. The local definition supplies its own finite-regulator and convergence conditions.

items.statement: Fix a smooth Lorentzian bulk spacetime $(M,g)$ and a supplied timelike conformal boundary. A **boundary Cauchy slice** is a smooth spacelike hypersurface of that boundary which every inextendible causal curve in the boundary meets exactly once. A **boundary region** $A$ is a relatively compact open subset of such a slice with smooth boundary $\partial A$. Fix a specified homology class $\mathcal H_A$ and a supplied class $\mathcal X_A$ (which may be empty) of smooth embedded codimension-two surfaces $X$, meaning $\dim X=\dim M-2$, with $\partial X=\partial A$. **Spacelike** means that the induced metric on $X$ is positive definite. Membership in $\mathcal H_A$ means that the model supplies an admissible bulk region $R_X$ whose relative boundary is $A\cup X$ on its chosen bulk Cauchy slice. The existence of any such surface is input data, not a consequence of this definition.
items.design_state: Step 1 local A-page definition added because the existing regulated generalized-entropy definition is restricted to a fixed null screen; this item supplies the finite AdS candidate-surface interface explicitly.

items.title: Restricted semiclassical entropy dictionary
items.physical_scope: An adopted entropy dictionary for one asymptotically locally AdS effective bulk model, one boundary state family supported on a finite-dimensional regulated code subspace, one boundary region and homology class, and one fixed regulator and renormalization scheme. It asserts no candidate existence, finite renormalized value, saddle dominance, universal boundary-to-bulk duality, or empirical validity.

references.title: Daniel Harlow, Jerusalem Lectures on Black Holes and Quantum Information, §§6.2.3 and 6.10
references.locator: Full-text lecture notes; §6.2.3 on the AdS/CFT dictionary and its semiclassical regime; §6.10, equations (195)–(196), on the leading-order RT/HRT proposal, anchoring, homology, and least-area selection.

references.title: Ahmed Almheiri, Thomas Hartman, Juan Maldacena, Edgar Shaghoulian, and Amirhossein Tajdini, The entropy of Hawking radiation, §§6, 8, 10, and 11.2
references.locator: Full-text review; §6, equation (6.2), for extremization followed by minimization of generalized entropy; §8, equation (8.2), for islands; §10, equation (10.4), for replica continuation; §11.2 for unresolved path-integral saddle, contour, cutoff, and exact-state limits.

items.statement: Fix an effective bulk model on a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ of dimension $d+1$, with $d\ge2$ and signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. Here AdS means anti-de Sitter. In this item, **asymptotically locally AdS** means that $M$ is the interior of a smooth manifold with boundary $\overline M$, and there is a dimensionless smooth defining function $z$ with $z>0$ on $M$, $z=0$ and $dz\ne0$ on $\partial\overline M$, such that $\overline g=z^2g$ extends smoothly to a nondegenerate metric whose induced boundary metric is Lorentzian. The model fixes its AdS length $L>0$ in metres, the asymptotic AdS boundary condition, bulk fields, semiclassical approximation, and conformal-boundary data; **semiclassical** here means that the bulk geometry is treated classically while the bulk entropy is computed from regulated quantum-state data on that geometry. No bulk field equation is inferred here.
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the assigned inventory; the boundary dictionary remains an adopted, restricted model premise.

items.title: Entropy transition in a specified two-candidate model
items.physical_scope: A conditional prediction for a boundary region whose prescribed candidate class consists of exactly two quantum-stationary surfaces with finite, continuously differentiable generalized-entropy branches on an open boundary time interval. The cusp is a property of the adopted minimum rule, not a deduction about an exact finite-cutoff microscopic entropy or about which saddle contributes in a different gravitational path integral.

references.title: Ahmed Almheiri, Thomas Hartman, Juan Maldacena, Edgar Shaghoulian, and Amirhossein Tajdini, The entropy of Hawking radiation, §§6 and 8
references.locator: Full-text review; §6, equation (6.2), and §8, equation (8.2), for extremize-then-minimize generalized-entropy prescriptions and competing contributions. The local theorem proves the two-branch transition directly.

items.statement:
Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open interval of boundary time, measured in seconds, and let $t_0\in I$. Suppose the prescribed candidate class in the dictionary of [[post-tgrx-semiclassical-ads-dictionary]] consists, near $t_0$, of exactly two admissible surfaces $X_1(t)$ and $X_2(t)$. title: AdS gravity entropy dictionary and quantum extremal surfaces — Examples

items.title: Replica saddles and islands retain their model assumptions
items.physical_scope: A source-based limitation on island and quantum-extremal-surface calculations in selected semiclassical gravity models. It records their regulator, state-factorization, replica-continuation, and gravitational-saddle assumptions; it asserts no empirical observation or theorem of microscopic unitarity for an unspecified four-dimensional black hole.

references.title: Ahmed Almheiri, Thomas Hartman, Juan Maldacena, Edgar Shaghoulian, and Amirhossein Tajdini, The entropy of Hawking radiation, §§8, 10, and 11.2
references.locator: Full-text review; §8, equation (8.2), and §10, equations (10.1)–(10.4), for the island prescription and replica continuation; §11.2 for the unresolved gravitational path-integral contour, saddle inclusion, cutoff, and exact-state issues.

references.title: Phil Saad, Stephen H. Shenker, and Douglas Stanford, JT gravity as a matrix integral, §§1 and 6
references.locator: Full-text article; §1 for the model-specific JT genus expansion and non-unique nonperturbative matrix-integral completion; §§6.1–6.3 for ensemble dependence, non-disordered theories, and open higher-dimensional questions.

items.statement: For selected semiclassical gravity-plus-bath models, an island or quantum-extremal-surface calculation uses a specified boundary state and region factorization, a regulator and renormalization prescription, and gravitational path-integral assumptions. The replica prescription for a density matrix $\rho$ computes $S=(1-n\partial_n)\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^n)|_{n=1}$ by analytic continuation from replica number $n$; the gravitational calculation must also specify which saddle configurations contribute and which dominates. A Page-like curve here means a model entropy profile that rises and later falls under its stipulated parameter evolution. Such a curve is a conditional prediction of that selected calculation; it does not establish microscopic unitarity of an unspecified four-dimensional evaporating black hole or prove that a candidate saddle contributes in another theory.
